text: On the Cessna 172R airspeed indicator, the lower limit of the white arc is what speed?

options.A: VFE - maximum flap extension speed (85 KIAS)
options.B: VSO - stall speed in the landing configuration at maximum weight (33 KIAS)
options.C: VS1 - stall speed with flaps up at maximum weight (44 KIAS)

explanation: The white arc is the full flap operating range. Its lower limit is VSO, the stall speed at maximum weight in the landing configuration (33 KIAS); its upper limit is VFE (85 KIAS).

text: What is the significance of the upper limit of the white arc on the Cessna 172R airspeed indicator?

options.B: VNO - maximum structural cruising speed (129 KIAS)
options.C: VFE - maximum speed permissible with flaps extended (85 KIAS)

explanation: The upper limit of the white arc is VFE, the maximum flap extended speed (85 KIAS). The white arc covers the full flap operating range from VSO (33 KIAS) to VFE (85 KIAS).

text: The lower limit of the green arc on the Cessna 172R airspeed indicator represents which speed?

options.A: VS1 - stall speed at maximum weight and most forward CG with flaps retracted (44 KIAS)
options.B: VSO - stall speed in the landing configuration (33 KIAS)
options.C: VNO - maximum structural cruising speed (129 KIAS)

explanation: The green arc is the normal operating range. Its lower limit is VS1 (44 KIAS), the stall speed at maximum weight and most forward CG with flaps retracted; its upper limit is VNO (129 KIAS).

text: The upper limit of the green arc on the Cessna 172R airspeed indicator is which speed?

options.B: VNO - maximum structural cruising speed (129 KIAS)
options.C: VFE - maximum flap extension speed (85 KIAS)

explanation: The upper limit of the green arc is VNO, the maximum structural cruising speed (129 KIAS). Above VNO lies the yellow caution range.

text: On the Cessna 172R, the red line on the airspeed indicator marks which speed?

options.A: VNO - maximum structural cruising speed (129 KIAS)
options.B: VA - maneuvering speed (99 KIAS at 2450 lb)
options.C: VNE - never exceed speed, above which structural failure may occur (163 KIAS)

explanation: The red line marks VNE (163 KIAS), the maximum speed for all operations. Above this speed, structural failure may occur.

text: How should operations within the yellow arc on the Cessna 172R airspeed indicator be conducted?

options.A: With caution and only in smooth air

explanation: The yellow arc (129 to 163 KIAS) is the caution range. Operations must be conducted with caution and only in smooth air.

text: On the G1000-equipped Cessna 172R, what does the red arc on the low end of the airspeed scale indicate?
explanation: On the G1000 airspeed indicator only, a red arc from 20 to 33 KIAS provides a low airspeed warning. The conventional steam-gauge 172R indicator does not display this arc.

text: What is VNE (never exceed speed) for the Cessna 172R?
explanation: VNE is 163 KIAS (160 KCAS). This speed must not be exceeded in any operation.

text: What is VNO (maximum structural cruising speed) for the Cessna 172R?
explanation: VNO is 129 KIAS (126 KCAS). Do not exceed this speed except in smooth air, and then only with caution.

text: What is the maneuvering speed (VA) of the Cessna 172R at 2450 pounds?
explanation: At 2450 lb, VA is 99 KIAS (97 KCAS). At 2200 lb it is 94 KIAS (93 KCAS), and at 1600 lb it is 82 KIAS (82 KCAS).

text: Which statement regarding maneuvering speed (VA) on the Cessna 172R is correct?

options.A: Above VA, full or abrupt control movements may overstress the airframe
options.B: VA remains constant regardless of aircraft weight
options.C: Above VA, flaps may be extended at any time

explanation: Do not make full or abrupt control movements above VA. VA decreases as aircraft weight decreases (99 KIAS at 2450 lb, 94 at 2200 lb, 82 at 1600 lb).

text: What is the maximum flap extended speed (VFE) with flaps FULL on the Cessna 172R?
explanation: With flaps at 10° the limit is 110 KIAS (108 KCAS). From 10° to FULL the limit is 85 KIAS (84 KCAS). Do not exceed these speeds with flaps down.

text: At what speed may the windows be left open on the Cessna 172R?
explanation: The maximum window open speed is 163 KIAS (160 KCAS). Do not exceed this speed with the windows open.

text: What engine powers the Cessna 172R?

options.A: Textron Lycoming IO-360-L2A rated at 160 BHP
options.C: Textron Lycoming O-320 rated at 150 BHP

explanation: The Cessna 172R is powered by a Textron Lycoming IO-360-L2A rated at a maximum of 160 BHP.

text: What is the maximum engine speed for the Cessna 172R?
explanation: The maximum engine speed is 2400 RPM for takeoff and continuous operations. The tachometer red arc runs from 2400 to 2700 RPM.

text: What is the maximum oil temperature limit for the Cessna 172R engine?
explanation: The maximum oil temperature is 245°F (118°C). The oil temperature indicator shows a green range of 100 to 245°F and a red arc from 245 to 250°F.

text: What are the minimum and maximum oil pressure limits for the Cessna 172R?
explanation: Oil pressure minimum is 20 PSI and maximum is 115 PSI. The indicator green arc is 50 to 90 PSI, with red arcs below 20 and above 115 PSI.

text: What is the normal operating range of the tachometer on the Cessna 172R?
explanation: The tachometer green arc is 1900 to 2400 RPM. The red arc runs from 2400 to 2700 RPM, with the maximum operating limit at the lower end of the red arc.

text: What is the total fuel capacity of the Cessna 172R?
explanation: Total fuel is 56.0 U.S. gallons, 28.0 gallons per tank. Usable fuel is 53.0 U.S. gallons (26.5 per tank), and unusable fuel is 3.0 U.S. gallons (1.5 per tank).

text: How much usable fuel does the Cessna 172R carry?
explanation: Usable fuel in all flight conditions is 53.0 U.S. gallons, 26.5 gallons per tank. Unusable fuel is 1.5 gallons per tank (3.0 total).

text: Which fuel grades are approved for the Cessna 172R?

options.A: 100LL Grade Aviation Fuel (blue) and 100 Grade Aviation Fuel (green)

explanation: Approved fuel grades are 100LL Grade Aviation Fuel (blue) and 100 Grade Aviation Fuel (green).

text: How much unusable fuel is in each Cessna 172R fuel tank?
explanation: Unusable fuel is 1.5 U.S. gallons per tank, or 3.0 U.S. gallons total. The fuel quantity indicator red line is at 0, with 1.5 gallons unusable in each tank.

text: What flap settings are approved for takeoff on the Cessna 172R?

options.C: None - flaps must be retracted for takeoff

explanation: The approved takeoff flap range is up to 10°. The approved landing flap range is up to FULL.

text: What is the oil capacity of the Cessna 172R engine?

options.B: 8 U.S. quarts in the sump, 9 U.S. quarts total

explanation: Oil capacity is 8 U.S. quarts in the sump and 9 U.S. quarts total.

text: What is the standard empty weight of the Cessna 172R?
explanation: The standard empty weight is 1639 pounds. Maximum useful load in the normal category is 818 pounds.

text: What is the maximum ramp weight of the Cessna 172R in the normal category?
explanation: Normal category maximum ramp weight is 2457 pounds, takeoff weight 2450 pounds, and landing weight 2450 pounds. Utility category limits are 2207/2200/2200 pounds.

text: What are the maximum takeoff and landing weights of the Cessna 172R in the normal category?
explanation: Normal category takeoff weight is 2450 pounds and landing weight is 2450 pounds. Ramp weight is 2457 pounds.

text: What airspeed should the pilot establish immediately after an engine failure after takeoff on the Cessna 172R?

options.A: 65 KIAS with flaps up, or 60 KIAS with flaps 10° to full, and land straight ahead

explanation: Immediately after takeoff, establish 65 KIAS with flaps up or 60 KIAS with flaps 10° to full, and land straight ahead.

text: What is the best glide speed for the Cessna 172R?
explanation: The best glide speed is 65 KIAS, which should be established during an engine failure in flight.

text: What are the first steps of the Cessna 172R engine restart procedure during flight after an engine failure?

options.A: Establish 65 KIAS, FUEL SHUTOFF valve ON, FUEL SELECTOR BOTH, FUEL PUMP ON, then Mixture RICH if restart has not occurred
options.C: Turn back immediately and force the restart

explanation: Establish 65 KIAS (best glide), then FUEL SHUTOFF valve ON, FUEL SELECTOR valve BOTH, FUEL PUMP ON, and Mixture RICH if restart has not occurred.

text: What is the first action for an engine fire IN FLIGHT on the Cessna 172R?
explanation: For an engine fire in flight: Mixture IDLE CUTOFF, FUEL SHUTOFF valve OFF, FUEL PUMP OFF, then MASTER Switch (ALT and BAT) OFF.

text: What is the first action when an electrical fire occurs in flight on the Cessna 172R?

options.A: STBY BATT switch OFF, then MASTER switch (ALT and BAT) OFF

explanation: For an electrical fire: STBY BATT OFF, MASTER (ALT and BAT) OFF, close cabin vents, turn cabin heat/air OFF, and activate the fire extinguisher if available.

text: What is the first step if icing is inadvertently encountered in flight on the Cessna 172R?
explanation: Turn PITOT HEAT ON, then turn back or change altitude to an outside air temperature less conducive to icing, and use maximum windshield defroster airflow.

text: What should the pilot do if a static source blockage is suspected on the Cessna 172R?

options.A: ALT STATIC AIR valve - ON (pull full out)

explanation: If erroneous instrument readings are suspected due to static source blockage, pull the ALT STATIC AIR valve ON (full out).

text: What is the first action if the CO LVL HIGH annunciator comes on during flight in the Cessna 172R?

options.A: CABIN HT control knob OFF, then CABIN AIR ON, vents and windows OPEN

explanation: For a high carbon monoxide level advisory: CABIN HT control knob OFF, CABIN AIR ON (pull full out), cabin vents OPEN, and cabin windows OPEN (max 163 KIAS windows open speed).

text: What is the first action during an engine fire that occurs during start on the ground if the engine STARTS on the Cessna 172R?

options.A: Continue cranking and set power to 1800 RPM for a few minutes
options.B: Set mixture to IDLE CUTOFF immediately
options.C: Turn the MASTER switch OFF immediately

explanation: For an engine fire during start with the engine running: continue cranking in START, and if the engine starts, set 1800 RPM for a few minutes, then shut down and inspect for damage.

text: What transponder code should be set if two-way radio communication is lost on the Cessna 172R?
explanation: Squawk 7600 for communication failure. 7700 is for emergencies (Mayday), and 7500 is for hijacking.

text: When communicating 'TRANSMITTING BLIND' after a radio failure in VMC, what should the pilot do when approaching the aerodrome?

options.A: Land straight in on any available runway
options.B: Approach side-on to the runway-in-use at 500 ft above traffic pattern and rock the wings
options.C: Circle the field at 1000 ft AGL and wait for a response

explanation: Approach the aerodrome side-on to the main runway at 500 ft above traffic pattern height, carry out a standard overhead circuit joining procedure, and rock the wings while flying in front of the tower.

text: If radio communication is lost in IFR conditions, at what altitude should the pilot maintain per 14 CFR 91.185?

options.A: The lowest altitude along the route
options.B: The highest of: last assigned altitude, minimum IFR altitude, or expected altitude
options.C: The filed flight plan altitude only

explanation: In IFR radio failure, maintain the HIGHEST of the last assigned altitude, the minimum IFR altitude for the route segment, or the altitude ATC advised may be expected in a further clearance.

text: What is the first step when lost under VFR on the Cessna 172R?

options.A: Land at the nearest suitable field immediately
options.B: Try to establish radio contact with any nearby ATC unit equipped with radar or VDF; if unsuccessful, make a PAN call on 121.50 MHz
options.C: Turn to a heading of 180° and fly until fuel is exhausted

explanation: First try to establish radio contact with any nearby ATC unit with radar or VDF. If unsuccessful, make a PAN call on 121.50 MHz. Then consider weather, light, fuel, climb for range, and fly a cardinal heading toward an identifiable feature.

text: When lost under VFR, what should the pilot fly toward to re-establish position?

options.B: A cardinal heading (N, S, E, or W) toward an identifiable line feature outside the circle of uncertainty
options.C: Directly toward the sun to use it as a compass reference

explanation: Fly a cardinal heading (N, S, E, or W) toward an identifiable line feature outside the circle of uncertainty, then fly along the feature until position can be fixed, and divert to the nearest suitable airfield.
